signature: „1741 MACHT. FRIEDRICH EHE IN NURNB”; master’s mark: “F * E”
remarks: two tubular slide stays, lower one telescopic; slide bow has ring and saddle, saddle has zigzag pattern; 1 flat bell stay with Nuremberg-style floral pattern, hinge, pin, eyelet (eyelet in center of flower), identical pattern on both sides of bell stay; ring and saddle in bell blow; garland has raised dots; floral pattern on garland; silver plating, applied and spread, on garland and bell stays. Part of a set with 1741-2 and 1741-3. Examined by the author, 15 August 2002. Dérans 1995 mentions 3 trombones (descant or alto, tenor and bass) signed 1741 and 1743).” The same source mentions “1 original case for the trombone, brownpainted [sic] exterior and redpainted [sic] interior with blue velvet. The case is meant for 4 trombones, a whole family, but the smallest one is missing.”
